1.why: /api/reset/verify rejects any token whose record.sessionId does not match the caller's session.id, so each reset code is checked against the session that requested it.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the requesting sessionId and deleted from resetRecords upon first successful verification, so the same code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: /api/password only replaces the global passwordHash and clears mfaVerified for the current session; no other entries in the sessions map are invalidated, so previous sessions keep working.

4.why: The app serves HTTPS via Bun TLS on port 3000 with HSTS and the HTTP port only issues a 308 redirect, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest (1.3).

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 verifiers and passwords as Argon2id hashes from CSPRNG material, though MFA codes are held in plaintext in session state.

6.why: No email message exists in this system; the simulated recovery token is returned in the HTTPS API response and displayed in a same-session testing log panel instead.

7.why: Contact input must match strict email/phone regexes, tokens must match a 64-hex pattern, JSON bodies are type-checked, and all client rendering uses textContent.

8.why: The sole redirect is a fixed-host HTTP-to-HTTPS 308 to https://localhost:3000, and all SPA links plus CSP form-action 'self' keep navigation on the hospital origin.

9.why: There are no email templates at all, and the page template and DOM code never interpolate user input into HTML (server-generated nonce/CSRF only, textContent elsewhere).

10.why: Error pages are generic, but recovery tokens and MFA codes are deliberately written to the on-page 'Logs' panel and console.log, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed with the initial hash supplied via environment variable, but the secret MFA codes '482913' and '741852' are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: No default password credential exists and login is impossible unless INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH is set (passwordHash.length > 0 check), though the fixed MFA codes act as shared secrets.

13.why: recordAttempt/blocked throttle recovery (3), verify/mfa/login/loginMfa (5) with a 60-second lockout, but counters are per-session and can be reset by obtaining a fresh session cookie.

14.why: /api/recovery returns the identical generic message with HTTP 200 for both invalid and valid contacts, so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: Reset codes are 256-bit CSPRNG-generated hex, stored only as SHA-256 digests, bound to the requesting session, single-use, and expire after 10 minutes.
